questions.prompt: Two lines meet at 90°. What do we call them?
questions.explanation: Lines that meet at 90° are perpendicular. Parallel lines never meet at all.

questions.prompt: Two angles sit on a straight line. One is 130°. What is the other?
questions.explanation: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°: 180 - 130 = 50. Taking 130 from 360 gives 230, but 360 is the rule for a full turn round a point.

questions.prompt: Two lines cross. One angle is 75°. What is the angle opposite it?
questions.explanation: Opposite angles are equal, so it is 75°. 105° is the angle next to it, not the one opposite.

questions.prompt: Three angles meet at a point. Two of them are 150° and 90°. What is the third?
questions.explanation: Angles at a point add up to 360°: 150 + 90 = 240 and 360 - 240 = 120. 240 is only the sum of the two you know.

questions.prompt: Two angles add up to 90°. One is 40°. What is the other?
questions.explanation: 90 - 40 = 50. Taking 40 from 180 gives 140, but these two angles make a right angle, not a straight line.

questions.prompt: Two lines cross and one angle is 60°. What is the angle next to it on the same straight line?
questions.explanation: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°: 180 - 60 = 120. 60° is the opposite angle, not the one next to it.
